record.paper_title: High Open-Circuit Voltages in Lead-Halide Perovskite Solar Cells – Experiment, Theory and Open Questions
record.original_question: How should non-radiative multiphonon recombination models for lead-halide perovskites be modified beyond harmonic-oscillator potentials so that transition rates between band-like states and localized defect states account for anharmonic fluctuations of lead-halide bonds and their effect on wavefunction overlap?

evidence.quote: These can be calculated for non-radiative processes using the theory for multiphonon recombination, which assumes that every downward transition between two states has to involve the emission of multiple phonons in order to dissipate the energy of the excited state.

Recently, it has been shown that the model of the harmonic oscillator for the potential energy of electrons and holes is insufficient to explain the magnitude and temperature dependence of the charge carrier mobility in lead-halide perovskites [92]. Instead, the anharmonic fluctuations of the lead-halide bonds affect the overlap of wavefunctions and thereby charge transport. In a similar way also the multiphonon recombination models that rely on harmonic oscillators to calculate transition rates between band like states and defect states likely have to be modified to the special case of lead-halide perovskites.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a semiconductor in which charge carriers can occupy delocalized band-like states (conduction band electrons and valence band holes) and localized defect states inside the band gap. Non-radiative recombination is described by multiphonon transitions: a downward electronic transition between two such states releases its electronic energy by simultaneous emission of multiple phonons of the host lattice. The standard theory (Huang–Rhys / Henry–Lang formalism) computes the transition rate using configuration-coordinate diagrams in which the adiabatic potential energy surfaces of both the initial and the final electronic state are approximated by harmonic oscillators with prescribed frequencies and equilibrium-position offsets, and the electron–phonon matrix element is evaluated from overlaps of harmonic oscillator vibrational wavefunctions weighted by a linear electron–phonon coupling.

Suppose now that the host lattice has the following non-standard properties, characteristic of lead-halide perovskites: (i) the metal–halide bonds undergo large-amplitude, strongly anharmonic thermal fluctuations on a timescale comparable to or slower than electronic motion; (ii) these anharmonic fluctuations dynamically modulate the spatial overlap of the electronic wavefunctions of band states and defect states; (iii) low-frequency optical phonon modes contribute non-perturbatively to the dissipation of electronic energy.

Formulate a generalization of the multiphonon non-radiative recombination rate that replaces the harmonic-oscillator vibrational basis and linear electron–phonon coupling with a model incorporating anharmonic ionic potentials and a fluctuation-dependent electronic overlap. Specifically, derive an expression for the temperature- and energy-dependent transition rate between a band-like state and a localized defect state in which:
(a) the ionic potential along the relevant configuration coordinate(s) is a general anharmonic potential rather than quadratic;
(b) the electronic matrix element depends explicitly on the instantaneous ionic configuration through the modulation of wavefunction overlap;
(c) the resulting rate reduces to the standard harmonic multiphonon expression in the harmonic, weak-modulation limit.

Determine how this modification quantitatively changes the predicted magnitude and temperature dependence of non-radiative recombination rates compared with the harmonic-oscillator result.
artifact.status_search_result: Several subsequent works have made progress on this problem. Ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics studies (Zhang et al., Sci. Adv. 2020) and time-domain DFT analyses have shown that low-frequency anharmonic phonons and lattice distortions reduce nonadiabatic electron–phonon coupling and electron–hole overlap, explaining defect tolerance. Methodological developments such as "Anharmonic multi-phonon nonradiative transition: An ab initio calculation approach" and recent Phys. Rev. Applied (2025) work on anharmonic lattice relaxation provide partial frameworks. However, a fully general, predictive analytic theory replacing the harmonic Huang–Rhys formalism for lead-halide perovskites is not yet established, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Low-frequency lattice phonons in halide perovskites explain high defect tolerance toward electron-hole recombination
status_evidence.snippet: Photogenerated carriers couple only with low-frequency phonons and electron-hole states overlap weakly, decreasing nonadiabatic coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Identifies that anharmonic low-frequency phonons control nonradiative recombination in halide perovskites, partially addressing the modification of multiphonon models.

status_evidence.title: Anharmonic multi-phonon nonradiative transition: An ab initio calculation approach
status_evidence.snippet: Ab initio approach for computing anharmonic multi-phonon nonradiative transitions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a methodology beyond harmonic oscillators for multiphonon transition rates.

status_evidence.title: Mitigation of nonradiative recombination by enhanced anharmonic lattice relaxation in mixed-anion perovskites
status_evidence.snippet: Nonradiative recombination caused by halogen vacancy is significantly mitigated by enhanced anharmonic lattice relaxation and softening.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work demonstrates anharmonic relaxation effects on defect-mediated recombination, contributing partial solutions.

status_evidence.title: Anharmonicity Extends Carrier Lifetimes in Lead Halide Perovskites at Elevated Temperatures
status_evidence.snippet: Anharmonic effects influence carrier lifetimes in lead halide perovskites.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms anharmonic modifications materially alter recombination predictions.
